{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''semi-Hilbert space''' is a generalization of a [[Hilbert space]] in [[functional analysis]], in which, roughly speaking, the [[inner product]] is required only to be [[positive semidefinite quadratic form|positive semi-definite]] rather than [[definite bilinear form|positive definite]], so that it gives rise to a [[seminorm]] rather than a [[norm (mathematics)|vector space norm]]. 

The quotient of this space by the kernel of this seminorm is also required to be a Hilbert space in the usual sense.
